name: Esmolol
high_alert_note: Not confirmed as high-alert on a source read; the institution's list governs.
summary: Short-acting intravenous beta-blocker for short-term control of ventricular rate in supraventricular tachycardia including atrial fibrillation and flutter, and other labelled uses. Nursing focus: hypotension, bradycardia, cardiac failure, airway disease, diabetes and abrupt discontinuation.

items.text: The label describes esmolol hydrochloride injection as a beta adrenergic blocker indicated for short-term treatment, including control of ventricular rate in supraventricular tachycardia including atrial fibrillation and flutter.
Monitor for signs and symptoms of cardiovascular adverse effects, and report them; any change to the infusion is made on the prescriber's or protocol's instruction.
Monitoring frequency and alarm limits follow the unit's protocol for this medicine.
The label calls for monitoring of heart rate and rhythm and for close monitoring, especially if the starting blood pressure is low.
Monitor serum electrolytes during esmolol therapy.
Hypotension can occur and is dose-related; patients with haemodynamic compromise or on interacting medicines are at particular risk, and severe reactions may include loss of consciousness.
The label warns of bradycardia and cardiac failure and says to monitor for cardiovascular adverse effects.
It may exacerbate reactive airway disease.
In diabetes it may mask symptoms of hypoglycaemia and alter glucose levels, so monitoring is advised.
Abrupt discontinuation may risk myocardial ischaemia in patients with coronary artery disease.

Beta blockers, including esmolol, have been associated with raised serum potassium and hyperkalaemia; the risk is higher in renal impairment, and intravenous beta blockers have caused life-threatening hyperkalaemia in patients on haemodialysis.
The most common adverse reactions are symptomatic hypotension (sweating, dizziness) and asymptomatic hypotension.
Escalate for hypotension, a slow heart rate, wheeze, breathlessness, chest pain or signs of heart failure.
Record the product and order checks, monitoring results, adverse events and escalation per unit standard.

monitoring.text: Monitor blood pressure, heart rate and rhythm continuously or at the unit's frequency.
Watch for wheeze or breathlessness in patients with airway disease.
Check blood glucose in patients with diabetes.
Report hypotension, bradycardia or heart failure signs immediately.
